label: 0049 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 48 windows): 0047 with three more slow slip events (off Choshi 2004–05, Shima 2017–18, Tokai 2024–25) and the 2003 Bungo Channel event lengthened to 2002–04, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0047 with the slow slip that window cross-validation supports in stability checks of the record. The 2003 Bungo Channel slow slip event is lengthened from its September–November 2003 main pulse to its published duration, October 2002 to March 2004, and three slow slip events are new: off Choshi on the Japan Trench (March 2004 to November 2005), beneath the Shima Peninsula (April 2017 to May 2018) and at Tokai (January 2024 to May 2025, the accelerating phase of the slow slip the Earthquake Research Committee reports since early 2022). Together they raise window cross-validation by 714. Their Mw: Bungo 7.01 (published about 7.1), Shima 6.57 (published about 6.5), Tokai 2024 6.61, and off Choshi 7.08, an upper bound because the slip is offshore, where its size scales with the prior. With them, year-to-year changes in background coupling are nearly as small as in runs on data with no change, and Tokai background coupling stays at 0.30–0.41 in 2024–25 instead of dropping to 0.06–0.22. Each episode slips at a uniform rate, so the 30 days after the 2003 Tokachi-oki earthquake, during the Bungo main pulse, fit worse than in 0047: the model falls short of the Bungo sites' eastward motion by about 80 mm/yr. Elsewhere the fit matches 0047. Coupling far outside −1 to 1 isn't a real value: it is episode strike-slip, or Kumamoto afterslip, divided by a small plate rate. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
